company: Tallybird is a fictional AI meeting notetaker for teams, sold with a product-led motion: a 14-day Team trial with no credit card, then Pro, Team, Business, or Free. Shared recaps bring in new workspaces.

messages.subject: Activation dip
messages.body: Activation dipped on the weekly dashboard. What is going on, and what do you need from me?

messages.subject: Calendar tickets
messages.body: More new users stuck on the calendar step this week. Several mention needing admin approval.

release.title: Onboarding v2: connect calendar first
release.notes: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

payload.headline: 7-day activation fell sharply for Microsoft-calendar workspaces after onboarding v2 forced calendar-connect-first; Google and no-calendar segments were flat

cause.does_not_prove: That this release caused the drop by itself, only that its timing aligns with the onset.

evidence.quote: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

cause.text: Tallybird shipped rel_0412 ('Onboarding v2: connect calendar first') on 2026-02-10, forcing calendar connection before anything else and removing the skip option; this lands at the start of the decline window (recent period begins 2026-02-09).

cause.does_not_prove: That microsoft-calendar users are inherently less likely to activate; the comparison is before vs. after within the same segment, not microsoft vs. other providers.
cause.text: In the calendar_provider=microsoft segment, activation_rate_7d fell from 0.3937 to 0.3061 (-22.25% relative, p=0.0), while google (p=0.838747) and none (p=0.281091) segments were not significant.

cause.does_not_prove: That the connect step itself is bug-free; it only shows the break happens after connect and before the first recorded meeting.
cause.text: Within calendar_provider=microsoft, calendar_connect_rate_1d rose +60.04% (0.3321 to 0.5315, p=0.0) after rel_0412, while first_meeting_rate_7d fell -14.84% (0.5248 to 0.4469, p=0.0) -- the earliest funnel step moving in the same direction as the activation decline.

cause.does_not_prove: That every affected workspace filed a ticket; 7 accounts is likely a fraction of the segment's activation loss, and ticket text alone doesn't confirm whether the failure is an OAuth scope issue, a tenant admin consent block, or a Tallybird-side bug.

evidence.quote: Is there a way to record a meeting without connecting my calendar? The Outlook step keeps failing with a permissions message.
The Tallybird bot didn't join my Teams call this morning. It was on my calendar. Can you check what happened?

cause.text: Support tickets from calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces after rel_0412 describe being stuck at the forced calendar-connect step with a permissions failure, and the notetaker bot not joining scheduled Teams meetings.

payload.cheapest_test: Flip a feature flag to restore the skip option / non-forced calendar connect for calendar_provider=microsoft only (leave rel_0412 on for google), and watch first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d for that segment over the next week.
payload.question: Did 7-day activation change in the last few weeks? If so, why?
payload.recommendation: Roll back or flag off rel_0412's forced calendar-connect-first flow for Microsoft-calendar workspaces specifically; it correlates with a 22% activation drop driven by a failure between calendar connect and first meeting, and support tickets confirm users are stuck on an Outlook permissions error with no way to skip.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: rel_0318 shipped two weeks before the decline window started and is not calendar-provider specific; the google segment (which includes Zoom-using workspaces) shows no significant change (p=0.838747), so a platform-wide join-speed change doesn't explain a Microsoft-only effect. meeting_platform is rejected as a dimension at the wrong grain for this metric, so this is ruled out via the calendar_provider grain rather than chased further.

evidence.quote: The notetaker joins Zoom calls about 20 seconds sooner.

ruled_out.text: The earlier Zoom-bot faster-join release (rel_0318, shipped 2026-01-27) caused the activation drop.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Whether the Outlook 'permissions message' failure is an OAuth scope issue, a tenant admin consent block, or a Tallybird-side bug in the connect flow.
How many affected Microsoft workspaces abandoned onboarding silently without filing a support ticket.
would_change_if: If first_meeting_rate_7d for microsoft workspaces recovers over the next week without any product change, rel_0412 may not be the cause.
If flagging off the forced-connect flow for microsoft does not restore first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d, the mechanism is not the onboarding change itself.

findings.claim: 7 microsoft-segment workspaces filed the cited permissions/no-show support tickets (voice_workspaces: 7, evidence value 7 for q_33b9b06c27c6).
findings.evidence: review.check numbers=fail: replaying q_33b9b06c27c6 returns 11 distinct workspaces, not 7.
findings.impact: The voice-of-customer count is understated by ~36%, which is a factual error in an otherwise-approved recommendation; it doesn't change the diagnosis (mechanism proof via first_meeting_rate_7d and calendar_connect_rate_1d shifts, segment-specific significance, and ruled-out rel_0318 all still hold) but every number in a packet must be correct before it reaches the PM.
findings.smallest_action: Update voice_workspaces and the two evidence values from 7 to 11 (or re-run the query and cite the correct count), then re-submit for check.

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces brings their activation back to baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: Microsoft first_meeting_rate_7d not back to its week 1 to 5 level for cohorts after the rollback

builds.message: Add flag microsoft_calendar_connect_skip (off by default, scoped to calendar_provider=microsoft) that restores the skip option on the calendar-connect step for that segment only, per bet_0001 / pkt_0001's approved rollback action for rel_0412.
builds.diff:
--- a/tallybird/flags.yaml
+++ b/tallybird/flags.yaml
@@ -11,3 +11,11 @@
   rules:
     - {plan: [business, enterprise]}
   description: The notetaker joins Microsoft Teams calls through the new bot. Beta for Business and Enterprise.
+
+microsoft_calendar_connect_skip:
+  enabled: false
+  rules:
+    - {calendar_provider: [microsoft]}
+  description: >
+    Rollback of rel_0412 for calendar_provider=microsoft only: restores the skip option on the
+    calendar-connect onboarding step. Everyone else keeps the forced connect-first flow.
--- a/tallybird/onboarding.py
+++ b/tallybird/onboarding.py
@@ -20,10 +20,17 @@
 
 
 def steps(user: dict, flags: Flags) -> list[Step]:
-    """The steps for this user, in order. `user` carries calendar_provider (google or microsoft) and plan."""
+    """The steps for this user, in order. `user` carries calendar_provider (google or microsoft) and plan.
+
+    When microsoft_calendar_connect_skip is on for this user (calendar_provider=microsoft), the
+    calendar-connect step is skippable again, rolling back rel_0412's forced connect for that segment.
+    Every other user still sees the connect-first, unskippable step exactly as today.
+    """
+    can_skip_connect = flags.is_on("microsoft_calendar_connect_skip", user)
     return [
         Step("calendar_connect", "Connect your calendar",
-             "Tallybird joins the meetings on your calendar and writes the notes for you."),
+             "Tallybird joins the meetings on your calendar and writes the notes for you.",
+             skippable=can_skip_connect),
         Step("welcome", "Welcome to Tallybird", "Here is what a recap looks like."),
         Step("first_meeting", "Record your first meeting", "Start a meeting, or paste a meeting link."),
     ]
--- a/tests/test_microsoft_calendar_connect_skip.py
+++ b/tests/test_microsoft_calendar_connect_skip.py
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+from tallybird.flags import Flags
+from tallybird.onboarding import steps
+from tallybird.screens import render_step
+
+MS_USER = {"calendar_provider": "microsoft", "plan": "pro"}
+GOOGLE_USER = {"calendar_provider": "google", "plan": "pro"}
+
+
+def test_flag_off_by_default_microsoft_still_forced():
+    flags = Flags.load()
+    assert not flags.is_on("microsoft_calendar_connect_skip", MS_USER)
+    first = steps(MS_USER, flags)[0]
+    assert first.id == "calendar_connect" and not first.skippable
+
+
+def test_flag_on_restores_skip_for_microsoft_only():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"microsoft_calendar_connect_skip": True})
+    ms_first = steps(MS_USER, flags)[0]
+    google_first = steps(GOOGLE_USER, flags)[0]
+    assert ms_first.id == "calendar_connect" and ms_first.skippable
+    assert google_first.id == "calendar_connect" and not google_first.skippable
+
+
+def test_flag_on_renders_skip_button_for_microsoft_only():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"microsoft_calendar_connect_skip": True})
+    ms_html = render_step(steps(MS_USER, flags)[0])
+    google_html = render_step(steps(GOOGLE_USER, flags)[0])
+    assert 'data-action="skip"' in ms_html
+    assert 'data-action="skip"' not in google_html
+
+
+def test_order_and_step_count_unchanged_for_everyone():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"microsoft_calendar_connect_skip": True})
+    for user in (MS_USER, GOOGLE_USER):
+        assert [s.id for s in steps(user, flags)] == ["calendar_connect", "welcome", "first_meeting"]

payload.does_not_prove: That the effect will last, or that the action was the only change in the period.

cause.mechanism: Onboarding v2 made calendar connect mandatory. About 45% of Microsoft calendar workspaces need admin consent, so they get stuck.

affected.funnel_step: calendar connect step -> first real meeting. Connect completion rises (everyone must try), while consent failures now block the first meeting

cause.secondary_effect: Fewer activations mean fewer shared recaps, so recap_link signups start dipping 1 to 3 weeks later.

findings.finding: Localizes the drop to Microsoft calendar workspaces, not to Teams as a meeting platform.
Names admin consent on the mandatory calendar step as the mechanism.
Cites tickets from 3 or more workspaces.
Computes activation on mature cohorts only (7 full days).
Bonus: sizes the cost in revenue, or flags the delayed viral-loop effect.

correct: Restore the skip option for Microsoft calendar workspaces (or roll back v2 for them), then retest v2 behind a flag with a fallback when consent is required.
Roll back v2 for everyone, then retest behind a flag with the fallback.
partial: Roll back without a retest plan.
wrong: No action by the end of week 8.
Blame the Teams bot, channel mix, or seasonality.

traps: Cohorts from the last 7 days are immature.
Microsoft calendar users skew toward Teams, so a meeting-platform slice points at Teams.
Support tags are noisy: only half of consent tickets are tagged integration.
